messages:
pagerbot: P0 ALERT — GPU pool 'inference-eu-w' OOMs and queue growth > 95% for 6m. autoscaler entering deadzone, not adding nodes. links: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/GPUpool/inference-eu-w, runbook: /runbooks/gpu-pool-capacity

pagerbot: metric snapshots: queue_length=142k, avg_latency=1.8s, throttle_rate=0.32, 5xx_rate=7%

tim_sre: oncall here. I'm looking at the autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated throttled scale attempts: `scale_attempts=0 requests_in_deadzone=12`

sam_infra: looks like `autoscaler.deadzone_ms` got bumped in last rollout to 120000 (2m) to avoid flip-flop. but we have a sustained spike — deadzone prevents further scaling. rolling back to 30s might help.

maya_prod: customers hit: several live deployments reporting 429s and slow responses. Support ticket volume rising. Jen, can you summarize customer impact?

jen_support: customers affected: acme-inc (prod), clearwave (staging->prod), 4 smaller single-tenant projects. Incidents: higher tail latency, intermittent 429s. Escalation already open with account teams.

ana_eng: (typo) ana_eng: suspected cause: continuous-batching rollout from PR#4821 changed `kv_prefix_cache` sharding and reduced hit rate. prefix cache misses mean more decoder work per request -> GPU memory churn -> OOMs. I pulled a histogram: prefix_cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% to 12% after deploy.

sam_infra: confirm: we have both a config drift (batching/kv changes) and autoscaler deadzone that combined to create an overload window.

tim_sre: immediate live mitigation plan: 1) force scale up + override autoscaler to bypass deadzone: `infractl gpu scale --pool inference-eu-w --target 12 --override-deadzone` 2) revert continuous-batching rollout (PR#4821) -> rollback to previous kv sharding 3) increase prefix cache TTL to improve hit rate 4) add temporary rate-limit per-customer to reduce queue.

sam_infra: executing step 1 now. running: 
```
infractl gpu scale --pool inference-eu-w --target 12 --reason "live mitigation - OOM spike" --override-deadzone
```

sam_infra: command returned OK, requesting new instances. provisioning ETA ~90s.

pagerbot: deploy-bot: new nodes joined, pool capacity now at 12. autoscaler still in deadzone but override keeps nodes. queue_length dropping to 68k.

maya_prod: good. start rollback of PR#4821? can we Canary revert?

ana_eng: starting revert now, creating a rollback deployment to previous continuous-batching config: `kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/continuous-batcher continuous-batcher=continuous-batcher:v2026-01-19`

ana_eng: rollback applied. Watch prefix cache hit rate and decoder allocation.

tim_sre: monitoring metrics: prefix_cache_hit_rate -> 40% and climbing. queue_length -> 22k. 5xx down to 2.1%. nice.

jen_support: customers: acme-inc reporting improved response times, but still seeing retries queued. notifying impacted accounts with ETA ~15m for full recovery.

sam_infra: will follow up with a config audit. We need to ensure autoscaler deadzone isn't globally bumped in rollouts. Perhaps add a canary gate for autoscaler parameter changes.

maya_prod: agree. create an action item now. @ana_eng can you open a postmortem and link the config diff + PRs that changed prefix cache sharding and continuous-batching? Include customer impact and rollback timeline.

ana_eng: on it. I'll include timeline, metrics, and the exact cache keys that mis-sharded. Also will add a perf test for prefix-cache hit rate to CI.

tim_sre: handoff: I'm going offline in 25m. Next oncall @sam_infra will own monitoring and follow-up. leaving notes: keep override until autoscaler re-enters normal logic and queue < 5k for 10m.

sam_infra: ack. I'll keep the override for 30m and then try to let autoscaler reclaim control once deadzone expires. I'll also lower `autoscaler.deadzone_ms` back to 30s in staging and watch canary.

jen_support: created a consolidated customer impact doc and sent external comms for major accounts. will post links here in a sec.

pagerbot: NOTE: incident severity set to P0 -> active mitigation. create PM for postmortem.

maya_prod: thanks all. follow-up action items: 
- ana_eng: postmortem + CI perf test for prefix cache (owner)
- infra: add autoscaler param canary guard and revert policy (owner: sam_infra)
- runtime: add monitoring alert for prefix_cache_hit_rate drop -> page at 10% delta (owner: ana_eng)
- support: customer comms summary (owner: jen_support)

sam_infra: adding todo: `#infra` board -> autoscaler-deadzone-guard.

tim_sre: leaving final note: root cause = simultaneous regressed continuous-batching config that reduced prefix cache hit rates + aggressive autoscaler deadzone introduced in a separate rollout. combo caused sustained GPU memory churn and prevented scale-up. mitigations: rollback, override scale, adjust TTLs, add canaries. Closing active mitigation in 12m if metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
